newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold traders record quiet day.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold traders record quiet day.

text.p: Hong Kong's gold ended slightly higher on Tuesday following quiet trade after opening firmer than New York's finish.
Dealers who earlier in the day predicted sluggish Asian trade proved spot on, with gold trapped between US$380.50 and $381.50.

"Not much trading activity was noted and most players were staying away from the lacklustre market," said a dealer at a local brokerage. "The trend is mixed in the immediate futures, with support at US$378 and resistance at US$381."
Bullion ended at US$380.80/381.30 per ounce against US$380.35/85 in New York.
Local gold ended HK$13 higher at HK$3,511 per tael. The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Society remained unchanged from its Monday fix at -5.
